capabilities.text: Put points in order along one line and add more with + Point, from two up to seven
capabilities.note: Opening state: A, B and C. '+ Point' is greyed out at seven; the page never goes below two. Where an added point goes (at the right end) is inferred, not seen.

capabilities.text: Remove a chosen point, including one in the middle, down to two points
capabilities.note: Each point box has its own remove button ('Remove A'). What happens to the two parts either side of a removed middle point (joined or dropped) was not seen.

capabilities.text: Rename a point, such as M for a midpoint, up to four characters
capabilities.note: Point name boxes: maxlength 4, placeholder '?'. Names are drawn in italic under the line. Example 'Midpoint of a segment' uses A, M, B.

capabilities.text: Leave a chosen point undotted, with its name still drawn
capabilities.note: Dots section: one checkbox per point, all on at the opening state; the summary then reads 'n of m dotted'.

capabilities.text: Label a part above the line with a number length, such as 12
capabilities.note: Parts are the pieces between neighbouring points (AB, BC). The label mode starts at Text.

capabilities.text: Label a part with an expression in one letter, such as 2x + 3, the letter drawn in italic
capabilities.note: Opening state: AB is 2x + 1 and BC is 3x − 4. Any one letter, not only x.

capabilities.text: Type a part's expression with brackets or a number fraction, such as 3(x − 2) or x/2, and it is still solved
capabilities.note: Not in the bullets or help. Read from the page's solver: brackets, a number times a bracket and division by a number are accepted. How x/2 is drawn on the figure was not seen.

capabilities.text: Type a part label that is neither a number nor an expression (such as ?), drawn as typed and left out of the check with a note
capabilities.note: Not in the bullets. The check panel then says '“?” isn’t a number or an expression like 2x + 3, so it’s left out' (or 'so it can’t be solved' when nothing else gives the letter).

capabilities.text: Put a blank line in place of a part's label for students
capabilities.note: Per part 'How AB is labeled': Text / Blank line / None. Example 'four points' has a blank line over QR.

capabilities.text: Leave a part with no label at all
capabilities.note: Label mode None. Example 'Line with four collinear points' has no lengths.

capabilities.text: Mark a part with one, two or three congruence ticks
capabilities.note: Per part 'Congruence ticks on AB': None / | / || / |||; None at the opening state. Ticks are separate from the label: a part can have both.

capabilities.text: Mark two different pairs congruent in one figure with different tick counts (| on one pair, || on another)
capabilities.note: The solver reads tick counts 1, 2 and 3 as separate groups, each giving its own equation.

capabilities.text: Draw a brace under the line from one point to a later one, labeled with a length, such as AC = 27
capabilities.note: Opening state: one brace under AC labeled 27.

capabilities.text: Choose where a brace starts and ends, from any point to any later one, not only the whole segment
capabilities.note: Each span row has 'starts at' and 'ends at' selects; the end list only offers later points.

capabilities.text: Draw up to three braces, overlapping ones stacked so they don't collide
capabilities.note: '+ Span' is greyed out at three. Example 'four points and overlapping segments': braces for PR, QS and PS.

capabilities.text: Label a brace with an expression in the letter, such as 5x − 1
capabilities.note: Not in the examples. The span box's placeholder is 27, but its label goes through the same solver as a part's.

capabilities.text: Put a blank line under a brace for students
capabilities.note: Span label mode Blank line. Example 'Midpoint of a segment with expressions' has a blank line under the AB brace.

capabilities.text: Draw a brace with no label
capabilities.note: Span label mode None. Example 'four points': PS is a brace left unlabeled.

capabilities.text: Remove a brace, down to no braces
capabilities.note: Each span row has 'Remove the span AC'. The perpendicular bisector example has no brace.

capabilities.text: Make a ray: an arrow on the right end, the left end stopping at its point
capabilities.note: Ends: Left end / Right end, each 'Stops at the point' (opening state), 'Arrow' or 'Line arrow'. The Ends summary then reads Ray.

capabilities.text: Make a ray pointing left: an arrow on the left end only
capabilities.note: Either end can carry the arrow on its own.

capabilities.text: Make a line: arrows on both ends
capabilities.note: Example 'Line with four collinear points'. The Ends summary reads Line.

capabilities.text: Choose the arrowhead's style on each end, a filled arrow or an open line arrow
capabilities.note: Options 'Arrow' and 'Line arrow' per end; mixed ends are allowed. The page's hint: 'Stopping at both points makes a segment; one arrow makes a ray, two a line.'

capabilities.text: Draw a line crossing the segment at a chosen point, such as the midpoint M, for a bisector
capabilities.note: 'Crosses at': No crossing line (opening state) or any point, end points included. Hint: 'A bisector crosses at the midpoint: give the parts either side the same ticks.'

capabilities.text: Name the crossing line, such as ℓ
capabilities.note: Name box: placeholder ℓ, up to four characters; empty at the opening state. Shown only once a crossing point is chosen.

capabilities.text: Set the crossing line's angle to the segment, from 20° to 160° in steps of 5°
capabilities.note: 'Angle (°)' number box, 90° when the line is first added; limits read from the page's control.

capabilities.text: At 90°, draw a right-angle mark where the line crosses, or turn it off
capabilities.note: 'Right-angle mark' checkbox, shown only at 90° and on by default. Example 'Perpendicular bisector of a segment'.

capabilities.text: Draw each part to scale from its length, or from the solved value of the letter, none shorter than a fifth of the longest
capabilities.note: Drawn lengths summary 'Worked out' at the opening state: AB = 13 and BC = 14 put B just left of the middle. FAQ: 'none shorter than a fifth of the longest'. What an unworkable part is drawn as (inferred: the average of the others) was not seen.

capabilities.text: Type how long each part is drawn, for a figure not drawn to scale
capabilities.note: Drawn lengths: one box per part, placeholder 'auto'; the summary then reads 'As typed'. A part left empty keeps its worked-out size.

capabilities.text: Turn the whole figure, from −90° to 90° in steps of 5°
capabilities.note: Turn slider, 0° (Level) at the opening state.

capabilities.text: Make the labels large
capabilities.note: Label size buttons on the figure toolbar: Large / Medium (opening state) / Small.

capabilities.text: Make the labels small
Write the equation each brace gives, such as AB + BC = AC, below the parts
capabilities.note: Opening state reads 'AB + BC = AC'. A brace over a single part gives no equation of its own. Shown in the settings panel, not on the figure. Owner's round-0 rule (2026-11-19): counts only when drawn on the figure's answer-key copy.

capabilities.text: Write the equation matching ticks give, such as AM = MB, below the parts
capabilities.note: FAQ: 'AM = MB for parts with the same ticks'. Three parts with the same ticks give AB = BC = CD. Owner's round-0 rule (2026-11-19): counts only when drawn on the figure's answer-key copy.

capabilities.text: Solve for the one letter and list its value and every part and brace length, such as x = 6 · AB = 13 · BC = 14 · AC = 27
capabilities.note: Opening state exactly as quoted. Points help: 'Labels in one letter are solved below as a check.' There is no student/answer switch: the figure never shows these values. Owner's round-0 rule (2026-11-19): counts only when drawn on the figure's answer-key copy.

capabilities.text: Work out the length of a blank or unlabeled part from a brace or matching ticks and list it, such as QR = 7 from PQ = 5 and PR = 12
capabilities.note: Read from the page's solver: a part with no number is filled from a brace when it is the only unknown under it, or from a part with the same ticks. Also braces with no label are summed from their parts. Owner's round-0 rule (2026-11-19): counts only when drawn on the figure's answer-key copy.

capabilities.text: Say when the labels don't agree: a brace that doesn't add up with all-number labels, or a solved letter that breaks another equation
capabilities.note: Merged from the classifier's 07e and 07f by the owner's round-0 review. Owner's round-0 rule (2026-11-19): counts only when drawn on the figure's answer-key copy.

capabilities.text: Say when the labels can't be solved: a length comes out 0 or less, more than one letter is used, or there is no equation to solve from (or the letter cancels)
capabilities.note: Merged from the classifier's 07g, 07h and 07i by the owner's round-0 review. Owner's round-0 rule (2026-11-19): counts only when drawn on the figure's answer-key copy.
